tasks.title: Autosave delay
tasks.statement: PX4 parameters were saved **{e} s** ago. You change a parameter with `param set`. After how many seconds does the autosave fire?
tasks.solution: `ParamAutosave::request()`: a delay of 0.3 s, but no more than one save per 2 s. Delay = max(0.3, 2 − t), where t is the time since the last save. For t ≥ 1.7 s it stays at 0.3 s.

tasks.title: Parameter file size
tasks.statement: PX4 storage gets **{a}** integer parameters and **{b}** float ones; the average name length is exactly **{L}** characters. What is the size of the BSON document in bytes?
tasks.solution: Document: 4 length bytes + the records + 1 terminating byte. A record: 1 type byte, the name, 1 zero byte and the value, 4 bytes for an int32 and 8 for a double (PX4 writes floats as double). Total 5 + a·(L + 6) + b·(L + 10).

tasks.title: Average load from the Uptime line
tasks.statement: At the bottom of the `top` output there is the line `Uptime: {t}s total, {i}s idle`. What is the average CPU load since power-on, in percent?
tasks.solution: Load = 1 − idle / total time. `load_mon` computes the `cpuload` topic the same way, only over the last interval. Compare it with `COM_CPU_MAX` = 95 %: the arming check trips when it is exceeded for more than 2 s.

tasks.title: How many messages listener prints
tasks.statement: You typed `listener sensor_combined -r {r}` without `-n`, and the topic publishes continuously. How many messages does the command print before it exits?
tasks.solution: `listener_main.cpp`: if `-n` is not given but `-r` is, the message count = 30 · rate, "30 seconds at the given rate". Without both options it prints one message.

tasks.title: Card headroom before the cleanup threshold
tasks.statement: A 16 GB card running PX4 1.17 has **{f} MiB** free. `logger status` shows an average write rate of **{r} KiB/s**. How many minutes of logging are left before the 300 MiB threshold below which the logger starts deleting old logs at its next start?
tasks.solution: `check_free_space()`: a threshold of 300 MiB (or 10 % of the card, if that is less). Headroom = (free − 300) MiB · 1024 / rate in KiB/s, then divide the seconds by 60. The cleanup runs once at logger start; below 50 MiB the log does not start. In 1.18.0 the rule is based on `SDLOG_ROTATE` and `SDLOG_MAX_SIZE` instead.
